151773.title: The Corpses of the De Witt Brothers
151773.creator: attributed to Jan de Baen

editorial.note: The ultimate humiliation: the nude, flayed corpses of Johan and Cornelis de Witt on public display in the Groene Zoodje, the execution ground on the Vijverberg in the middle of The Hague.

Together, the two paintings hanging side by side here tell a story. In this one, a magnificent peacock wants to be king of the birds. Meanwhile, the magpie taking centre stage in the other painting voices its objection.

151927.title: A Pelican and other Birds near a Pool, Known as ‘The Floating Feather’
151927.creator: Melchior d'Hondecoeter

editorial.note: It must have been a great honour for Hondecoeter to receive commissions from the country’s ruler. He made this regal bird scene for Het Loo, the palace of William and Mary.

151928.title: A Hunter’s Bag near a Tree Stump with a Magpie, Known as ‘The Contemplative Magpie’
151928.creator: Melchior d'Hondecoeter

editorial.note: Commissioned by King William III of Orange, d’Hondecoeter painted these two hunting still lifes for Soestdijk Palace. They hung facing one another in a corridor whereby the magpie in this painting ‘speaks’ to the peacock in the other one.

Presented here are two squirrel monkeys from Central America, two white sulphur-crested cockatoos from Australia, a grey parrot from Africa and a purple-naped lory – on a chain at the lower left – from Indonesia.

152012.title: A Hen with Peacocks and a Turkey
152012.creator: Melchior d'Hondecoeter

editorial.note: Hondecoeter enlivened his bird paintings with little vignettes. Here the focus is on the hen taking care for her chicks, surrounded by large and intimidating birds.

152046.title: A Eurasian Eagle-Owl with Other Birds in a Landscape
152046.creator: attributed to Dirk Valkenburg

editorial.note: Even though owls are night predators, this eagle-owl has managed to catch a chicken during the day. It looks up angrily from his prey while being harassed by a wood pigeon.

152067.title: Hunting and Fruit Still Life next to a Garden Vase, with a Monkey, Dog and two Doves, in the distance Rijksdorp near Wassenaar, Seat of Jacob Emmery, Baron of Wassenaar
152067.creator: Jan Weenix

editorial.note: Jan Weenix (1642 - 1719). Still life with the estate of Rijksdorp in the background, 1714. The game and the birds provide proof of a successful hunt. The estate in the background is the country house Rijksdorp, near Wassenaar.

152212.title: Still Life with a Hare and other Game
152212.creator: Jan Weenix

editorial.note: Weenix set this luxurious game still life in the park of a country estate. He rendered the soft fur of the hare and the stiff wings of the partridge with his finest brushes. At the right are a hunting horn and a bag.

152329.title: Forest Floor Still Life with Birds, Butterflies and a Lizard
152329.creator: Melchior d'Hondecoeter

editorial.note: D’Hondecoeter specialized in painting birds, which he portrayed as lifelike as possible, such as the chaffinch at the upper right in this still life.
